confidence_notes: I did 3 web searches: one for the RBA rate and two for Mérida prices. The food and drink figures come from cost-of-living aggregators such as Expatistan, TravelTables, MyLifeElsewhere and Livingcost, plus Yucatán Today bar guides. These sources often disagree and some data is from 2023, so I took midpoints and allowed a little for prices rising by July 2026. Draft beer is cited at about MXN 50-60 (about USD 2.75-3), cappuccino at about USD 2.50-3.70, inexpensive meals at about USD 4.50-10 and mid-range meals for two at about USD 19-37. Cocktail pricing rests on one April 2026 bar guide that listed mezcal cocktails at MXN 145-160. Ordinary cocktails are cheaper, so I used about MXN 120-130. I found no per-glass wine prices. The wine estimate of about MXN 100 is based on its usual price relative to beer and a bottle price of about MXN 237, which is low-reliability data. The five accommodation figures are general-knowledge estimates only and were not checked against live listings or searches. July is the hot low season in Mérida, so room rates may be at or below these figures.
comparable_city_reasoning: Mérida is a mid-sized colonial city in Mexico with growing tourism and expat demand. Prices are generally a little below Mexico City and well below beach resorts such as Cancún and Tulum. Oaxaca City and Puebla are similar for hostel and three-star hotel pricing.
